channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Hackers force defrost on refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets; Danfoss confirms legacy units hit
item.category: Top Story
item.description: Attackers remotely forced refrigeration controllers at French supermarkets into defrost from the evening of 11 October, heating cabinets to as much as 50°C, starting fires at some stores and ruining fresh and frozen stock. Retailers confirm the hits: at least 300 Intermarché/Netto shops, more than 100 Coopérative U outlets, 80 Carrefour stores, about 5% of Monoprix and several E.Leclerc stores. Paris prosecutors call it large-scale and ANSSI is investigating; an unnamed source says it found a flaw in Danfoss software, while Danfoss says a limited number of legacy or outdated-firmware units were affected. Intermarché’s chief executive says one-day losses could reach tens of millions of euros. SecurityWeek and a Sekoia analyst say Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Spain were also hit (unconfirmed). No actor or entry route is confirmed. - Industrial Cyber (13 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera/AFP (13 Oct 2026); ABC News/AFP (updated 13 Oct 2026); CBS News/AFP (12 Oct 2026); Euronews (12 Oct 2026); Cooling Post, Danfoss statement (12 Oct 2026); Claroty Team82 Danfoss research (9 Aug 2026) - Attack from the evening of 11 Oct 2026; updated 13 Oct 2026 — investigation ongoing, details still emerging

item.title: [Critical] A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
item.category: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported
item.description: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779; the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and stolen configurations, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS 9.5) is a SAML memory overflow that could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but appliances patched last week need another upgrade. Shadowserver counts roughly 21,000 internet-exposed NetScaler fingerprints. Because NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, an unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT. - Citrix security bulletins CTX697096 and CTX697174 (and the 9 Oct bulletin for CVE-2026-107406); CISA KEV catalog; Dutch NCSC; Tenable, watchTowr, LevelBlue, Arctic Wolf and Mandiant/GTIG research; reported by SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - Fourth flaw CVE-2026-107406 patched 9 Oct 2026, no exploitation reported (The Hacker News, 9 Oct); CVE-2026-88779 fixed 3–4 Oct and added to KEV 4 Oct 2026 (deadline 7 Oct, now passed); watchTowr denial-of-service finding and CISA/Australian warnings 5 Oct 2026 (SecurityWeek and The Record, 5 Oct); first two flaws confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026, mass exploitation after a 28 Sep proof-of-concept write-up; post-exploitation analysis 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Ahold Delhaize reports a cybersecurity incident that took down Albert Heijn and Delhaize online services
item.category: Incident — Ahold Delhaize confirms a cybersecurity incident disrupting Albert Heijn and Delhaize online services in the Netherlands and Belgium; store-level OT impact not confirmed; no actor named
item.description: Ahold Delhaize said a cybersecurity incident began on Sunday 11 October, and it switched off some systems as a precaution. Albert Heijn websites, apps and customer service were unavailable, online deliveries paused and loyalty systems stopped; press reports add that some electronic shelf labels showed the previous week’s promotional prices. Delhaize customers in Belgium could not place new online orders. The company is investigating and putting customer, employee and partner data first. No actor has been named, and nothing public links the incident to the French refrigeration attacks, so the two are treated as separate for now. - Ahold Delhaize statements as reported by Hackread (12 Oct 2026) - Disruption began Sun 11 Oct 2026; reported 12 Oct 2026 — investigation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It is the other confirmed US case of OT tampering in this edition (see the French refrigeration top story), with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement (18 Sep 2026), reported by Axios Denver and Industrial Cyber (22 Sep) - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [High] Hackers reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system, Bloomberg reports; the FBI says there was no disruption
item.category: Incident — Bloomberg reports, citing unnamed US officials, that hackers temporarily reached the propulsion system of the US-bound tanker VL Prosperity; FBI on record: no operational disruption, instability or crew danger; actor, duration and extent of control unknown; a second tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials who asked not to be named, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had temporarily accessed the propulsion system of the very large crude carrier VL Prosperity as it approached the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact, and Bloomberg says it is unclear how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control. No one has been publicly blamed. VL Prosperity was boarded in the Atlantic on 21 August after it lost communications, and a second, unnamed tanker was boarded in the Gulf of Mexico days later. On 6 October a federal official told BankInfoSecurity that both boarded tankers were reached through known, unpatched flaws in onboard systems (single unnamed-official account, not independently confirmed). - Bloomberg (citing unnamed US officials), via Supply Chain Brain and gCaptain; FBI statement; boarding details per the US Coast Guard, Dragos and Reuters - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-system access reported 2 Oct 2026; unpatched-flaw detail reported 6 Oct 2026 (BankInfoSecurity)

item.title: [Medium] South African air traffic provider finds ransomware-associated malware in an airport weather-services OT network
item.category: Incident — South Africa’s air traffic provider ATNS found ransomware-associated malware in a weather-services OT environment at Port Elizabeth airport; contained, no disruption reported; China-linked data exfiltration is suspected, not confirmed
item.description: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa’s state-owned air traffic provider, disclosed malware of the kind usually seen early in ransomware attacks inside an operational-technology environment that supports weather services at Port Elizabeth airport, with East London airport possibly affected. Reports published 30 September and 2 October say ATNS believes its team contained and removed the infection and describe no flight or service disruption. Network monitoring suggested possible data exfiltration to addresses in China, but that is unconfirmed, no group has been named, and ATNS is hiring forensic investigators to establish how the intruders got in and what was taken. A separate insider data-theft allegation at another airport is being looked at and has not been substantiated. The case shows weather, navigation and airfield support systems are reachable targets. - ATNS disclosures as reported by SC Media (citing Dark Reading) and MyBroadband - Reported 30 Sep 2026 (SC Media) and 2 Oct 2026 (MyBroadband); investigation ongoing

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
item.category: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 7 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and SOCRadar’s latest count is 86,644 compromised devices. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary. - FBI and US Secret Service warning, reported by The Hacker News, BleepingComputer and The Record; CISA mitigation guidance (June 2026) - Ongoing — re-warned 7 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek follow-up on admin lockouts 8 Oct 2026; campaign first documented June 2026

item.title: [Info] Palo Alto survey: legacy OT and tool sprawl leave critical infrastructure exposed
item.category: Research — Palo Alto Networks 2026 State of Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity report (survey of more than 1,600 security leaders in 11 countries); vendor-run and self-reported; no CVE
item.description: A Palo Alto Networks survey of more than 1,600 critical-infrastructure security leaders, reported by Industrial Cyber on 10 October, finds that around 60% had a significant breach in the past year, and that most of those saw real impact such as downtime or production loss. Respondents said they lack full real-time visibility of OT assets (68%), named legacy, unpatchable equipment as their top risk (42%), and use an average of seven separate security tools. Only 26% have fully integrated IT and OT security operations. The company also cites 29% of 2026 CVEs being exploited within a day, against an industry average of 55 days to patch. The figures are self-reported and vendor-run, so treat them as directional rather than measured incident rates. - Palo Alto Networks 2026 State of Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity report, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Reported 10 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] FBI takes down domains behind Flax Typhoon’s scanning and phishing tools used against energy and airport targets
item.category: Threat Intelligence — FBI seizes seven domains behind the MicroScan and FishHub tooling of China-linked Flax Typhoon; joint FBI, CISA, NSA advisory lists power, gas and airport targets; no OT compromise confirmed
item.description: On 8 October the FBI announced it had seized seven domains used to run two hacking tools, MicroScan and FishHub, attributed to the China-linked group tracked as Flax Typhoon (also Ethereal Panda). MicroScan is a Python scanner with more than 1,300 testing scripts, used alongside a Mirai botnet; FishHub handles spear-phishing, malware delivery and data theft. A joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory (AA26-281A) with international partners lists targets that include a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, and Taiwanese gas and electricity firms, though the FBI did not confirm those were breached. Confirmed compromises are limited to Taiwanese universities. The advisory names older vulnerabilities such as CVE-2019-11510 (Pulse Secure VPN) and CVE-2021-22205 (GitLab). Authorities tie the actor to China-based Integrity Technology Group; they note not all activity may be linked to it. No operational-technology intrusion is described. CISA has since added five of the older flaws the group exploited to its KEV catalog, with an 11 October federal deadline. - FBI action and joint FBI/CISA/NSA advisory AA26-281A, reported by BleepingComputer, The Hacker News and Industrial Cyber - Announced 8 Oct 2026; KEV additions with 11 Oct deadline reported 9 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Unit 42 ties the Blinder Tunnel campaign to an Iran-aligned actor targeting aviation and telecoms
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Unit 42 attributes the Blinder Tunnel campaign (CL-STA-1178) to an Iran-aligned actor with high confidence; fake-recruitment lures against an Iraqi infrastructure engineer; telecoms and aviation named as wider targets; no OT or ICS compromise described
item.description: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 reports that a campaign it tracks as CL-STA-1178 used a fake recruitment process, imitating Dubai Airports IT, to hand an engineer in Iraq’s critical-infrastructure sector a trojanized coding test. Opening the project in the developer tool loaded malware that disabled event tracing and used GitHub comments as a hidden command channel. Wider targeting covers telecommunications and aviation in Iraq, Israel and the UAE, and a separate phishing campaign hit an Israeli entity in May and June. The activity is IT-focused, on developer workstations, and the report describes no OT intrusion. For defenders, the lesson is that engineers with plant or network access are being approached directly through job-themed lures. - Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 research, reported by Industrial Cyber - Reported 9 Oct 2026; campaign activity Nov 2025 to Jun 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco fixes critical remote code execution flaws in Nexus data-center switches and its license manager
item.category: Advisory — Cisco NX-OS on Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches (standalone mode), five remote code execution flaws, plus four flaws in Cisco License (Smart Software Manager); Cisco reports no known exploitation
item.description: On 7 October Cisco published fixes for five flaws in NX-OS on Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches running in standalone mode (CVE-2026-76471, -76485, -76486, -76501 and -76465). A crafted request or packet could give an attacker root code execution, or crash and reload the switch. Each depends on a feature being enabled — NX-API, NGOAM or MPLS OAM — and NX-API and MPLS OAM are off by default. A separate set of four flaws in Cisco License (Smart Software Manager) includes CVE-2026-76482 at CVSS 10.0 and CVE-2026-76480 at 9.8; the fix is version 10-202609, with no workaround, and older releases will not be patched. Cisco found the flaws in its own testing and knows of no attacks. In our assessment these switches commonly sit in the data-center and plant-backbone networks that carry OT traffic. - Cisco Security Advisory cisco-sa-moam-rce-uBTzYV7 and companion NX-OS and Cisco License advisories; reported by BleepingComputer (8 Oct) and relayed in the Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News digest (10 Oct) - Advisories published 7 Oct 2026; no exploitation reported

item.title: [High] CISA warns of a critical flaw in end-of-life Hitachi Energy RTU500 firmware that allows unauthenticated firmware uploads
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-279-06, Hitachi Energy RTU500 series CMU firmware (substation/utility remote terminal units); reported critical, unauthenticated firmware upload; end-of-life firmware branch; no known exploitation reported
item.description: On 6 October CISA published ICSA-26-279-06 for the CMU firmware of Hitachi Energy’s RTU500 series, widely used as remote terminal units in substations and other utility field sites. A digest of the release describes a critical flaw in an end-of-life firmware branch that lets an unauthenticated party upload firmware, which would mean arbitrary code on a device that talks to the control center. The same release also covered Hitachi Energy Asset Suite, SOI and REB500. We have not confirmed a CVSS score or CVE IDs from the advisory itself, so none are given here; check the advisory for affected versions. CISA reports no known exploitation in the digest we reviewed. End-of-life status matters: if your fleet runs the affected branch, the fix may be migration rather than a patch. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-279-06 (bulletin of six advisories, 6 Oct 2026), relayed by the IT/OT Security Weekly digest (11 Oct 2026) - Released 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA warns of seven flaws in Red Lion N-Tron 700 Series industrial switches, including hard-coded credentials and an authentication bypass
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-281-01, Red Lion Controls N-Tron 700 Series managed industrial Ethernet switches; seven vulnerabilities including hard-coded credentials and authentication bypass; no known exploitation reported
item.description: On 8 October CISA published ICSA-26-281-01 for Red Lion’s N-Tron 700 Series managed Ethernet switches, which sit in the network layer of plants, substations and water facilities. Per a digest of the advisory, firmware 3.11.0 and earlier (and bootloader 2.0.6.1 and earlier) contain seven flaws, among them hard-coded credentials and an authentication bypass that could hand an attacker administrative control of switch configuration. The advisory also describes a URL-triggered reboot that could be scripted, which is a potential outcome rather than a reported incident. Red Lion’s fix is firmware 3.11.1 or later. CISA reports no known public exploitation. Switch compromise matters because it can expose or reroute traffic between controllers and HMIs; we have not confirmed CVSS scores or CVE IDs from the advisory, so none are given here. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-281-01 (bulletin of six advisories, 8 Oct 2026), relayed by the Viakoo/Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News (11 Oct 2026) - Released 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA flags high-severity flaws in Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian grid-data software
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-281-02, Grid Protection Alliance openPDC and openHistorian (energy-sector grid data software); CVSS v3 9.8 as reported; no known exploitation
item.description: On 8 October CISA published ICSA-26-281-02, covering several classes of high-severity vulnerabilities in the Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian, open-source software that utilities use to collect and store time-series grid measurements (our description; CISA lists the energy sector). Trade coverage reports a vendor-equipment CVSS v3 score of 9.8, which is the figure to confirm against the advisory itself. CISA reports no known public exploitation. The relevance for OT teams is that these servers sit between substation or phasor data sources and control-center analytics, so a flaw there is a possible stepping stone between networks rather than a direct control-loop risk. Affected versions and fixes are listed in the advisory and are not repeated here. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-281-02, relayed by the Viakoo/Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News roundup (9 Oct 2026) - Released 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco warns of a fifth SD-WAN zero-day this year: an authentication bypass in SD-WAN Manager is being exploited
item.category: Advisory — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504, Cisco CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; fixed releases available; added to CISA KEV 30 Sep 2026 with a 3 Oct federal deadline, now passed; advisory revised 2 Oct; exploiting actor not named
item.description: Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504, a flaw in how Catalyst SD-WAN Manager handles URI encoding, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass an authentication rule protecting an API endpoint and gain administrator-level access. Cisco rates it CVSS 9.8, says it became aware of active exploitation in September without naming an actor, and lists no workarounds. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 3 October federal deadline, now passed, and Cisco revised its advisory on 2 October. Fixed releases exist for each supported train; releases older than 20.9 must migrate. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth SD-WAN zero-day exploited in 2026. In our assessment (editorial, not from the source), SD-WAN managers often control the WAN links that tie remote substations, plants and pipeline sites back to headquarters, so administrator takeover is a path toward those sites. - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer - Disclosed and added to KEV 30 Sep 2026; advisory revised 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet confirms an exploited FortiMail zero-day, and its updated advisory now lists fixed releases
item.category: Advisory — Fortinet FortiMail path-traversal / NULL-byte zero-day (CVE-2026-104286, Fortinet CVSS 9.8) exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 1 Oct 2026 (deadline 4 Oct); Fortinet’s 5 Oct update lists fixed releases
item.description: Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-175 describes a path-traversal and NULL-byte handling flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on a FortiMail appliance through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests. Fortinet scores it CVSS 9.8 and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA added it to KEV on 1 October with a three-day federal deadline. Affected branches are 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 8.0. When the advisory first appeared the fixes were only planned, but Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2, and tells 7.2 users to move to the 7.4 branch or later. In our assessment (editorial), FortiMail is an email gateway rather than an OT product, but it sits in the corporate trust zone that many plant networks inherit accounts and mail relays from, so a compromised gateway is a stepping stone worth closing off. - Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-175; CISA KEV catalog; reported by SecurityWeek - Disclosed and added to KEV 1 Oct 2026; fixed releases listed in Fortinet’s 5 Oct 2026 update

item.title: [Critical] Two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts against SonicWall’s maximum-severity SMA1000 flaw, days after hotfixes shipped
item.category: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, an SSRF in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated and remote; two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts (not confirmed successful); not in CISA KEV as of 12 Oct
item.description: Previdian and Defused both report their honeypots receiving requests consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10), a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 WorkPlace interface that SonicWall patched on 6 October; Defused dates its first hits to 8 October (SecurityWeek, 12 October). Neither has determined whether any attempt succeeded, and SonicWall’s advisory did not flag active exploitation. Fixed builds are 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670. The flaw is reachable remotely without authentication on SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected. Shadowserver counts more than 400 exposed SMA1000 appliances. The same interface was hit by SSRF flaws in July and September that were exploited, so quick scanning after a patch is plausible. These gateways often give vendors and integrators a path toward plant networks. - SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0017; Previdian and Defused honeypot observations, reported by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer; Shadowserver exposure data - Exploitation attempts reported 9–12 Oct 2026 (first seen 8 Oct); hotfixes released 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] One crafted packet can crash TDengine, a time-series database used in industrial data pipelines; a fix has existed since April
item.category: Advisory — TDengine time-series database, CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5): one unauthenticated packet to the default RPC port can crash the server; fixed in 3.4.1.6; no exploitation or public exploit reported
item.description: Researchers at Ridge Security found an integer-underflow bug in how TDengine parses messages before authentication. An attacker with network access to TCP port 6030 can crash the server with a single packet, which in an industrial setting means lost telemetry and dashboards that go blank rather than any change to a control loop. Versions 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5 are affected and 3.4.1.6 fixes it. Dark Reading corrected its first report on 30 September to say this is not an unpatched zero-day: the vendor advisory dates to 4 June and the patch has been available since April. Ridge holds a proof of concept but has not published it, and no in-the-wild attacks are reported. The practical risk is embedded or appliance-bundled copies that are hard to update. - Dark Reading, citing Ridge Security research and the TDengine advisory - Published 28 Sep 2026; corrected and updated 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] Industry coalition asks CISA for a binding directive on OT security inside federal agencies
item.category: Policy — OT Cybersecurity Coalition urges CISA to issue a binding operational directive on OT security at federal agencies; a proposal only, no CISA commitment; no CVE
item.description: The OT Cybersecurity Coalition is urging CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive focused solely on operational technology at federal civilian agencies, CyberScoop reported on 6 October. The coalition wants each agency to name an accountable OT cybersecurity officer, meet minimum practices drawn from existing federal guidance and CISA’s 2022 Cybersecurity Performance Goals, and consider whether NSA’s OT guidance should apply to civilian agencies. It points to a 30 September GAO report finding that only 7 of 22 civilian agencies fully met OMB’s requirements for networked IoT and OT devices, and to this summer’s water-utility attacks. CISA did not respond to CyberScoop and has announced no directive. In our assessment, a directive would bind only federal agencies but would signal what CISA expects of OT programs generally. - OT Cybersecurity Coalition paper, reported by CyberScoop; GAO-26-108937 - Reported 6 Oct 2026; GAO report 30 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] European energy bodies warn that AI and connected solar and battery devices are widening grid cyber risk
item.category: Policy — European energy-sector cybersecurity forum (E.DSO, EE-ISAC, ENCS, ENISA) flags AI, geopolitics and connected home energy devices as growing grid risks; no CVE
item.description: At the ninth Cybersecurity Forum in Brussels, organised by E.DSO, EE-ISAC, ENCS and ENISA (Industrial Cyber, 12 October), speakers said geopolitical attacks, AI and the spread of connected energy devices are adding risk that regulation alone cannot close. They pointed to the coordinated December 2025 attacks on Poland’s energy sector, which cut communications between facilities and grid operators, and to research showing that a compromised home router or camera could reach residential solar inverters and batteries, some of which accept commands without checking the sender. ENISA’s Threat Landscape 2026 reviewed 8,257 incidents from 2025. Recommendations include independent testing weighted by the power each device can move, vendor vulnerability management duties, and faster NIS2 and Network Code implementation. These are forum statements and research findings, not a newly confirmed incident. - Industrial Cyber report on the 9th Cybersecurity Forum (E.DSO, EE-ISAC, ENCS, ENISA) - Reported 12 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] NSA publishes zero-trust guidance for hardening critical OT environments
item.category: Guidance — NSA cybersecurity information sheet applying zero-trust principles to critical OT environments; aimed at defense and national-security systems but useful to any operator; no CVE
item.description: The NSA released a cybersecurity information sheet on 8 October that lays out how to apply zero-trust principles to critical operational technology. Its core idea is to assume a breach may already exist and to keep verifying users, devices, workflows and communications rather than trusting anything on the plant network. It is written mainly for owners and operators of national security systems, defense and the defense industrial base, but it also covers the added attack surface from bringing advanced AI into OT and notes that adversaries increasingly aim to disrupt or destroy critical infrastructure in sectors such as energy and water. WaterISAC has circulated it to the water sector. In our assessment, it gives other operators a ready reference for segmentation and access-control projects, though it is guidance, not a requirement. - NSA press release and cybersecurity information sheet; circulated by WaterISAC - Released 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST drafts a major update to its OT security guide, and CISA and the FBI advise limiting ICS integrator access
item.category: Guidance — NIST draft SP 800-82 Rev. 4 (Guide to OT Security), comments open to 30 Nov 2026; plus a CISA and FBI fact sheet on limiting ICS integrator access; no CVE
item.description: The week of 24 September NIST released a draft of Special Publication 800-82 Revision 4, its guide to operational technology security, with public comments due 30 November 2026. The draft is organized around the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, puts risk management under the Govern function, and adds sector coverage for building automation, water, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime vessels. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero trust. Around the same date CISA and the FBI published a fact sheet urging owners to give ICS integrators only the minimum access they need, write security and remote-access terms into contracts, and log vendor connections; it cites a 2025 breach of an automation company serving utilities and transport in which attackers staged 800 network schematics and device configurations. Both items are guidance, not requirements. - NIST draft SP 800-82 Rev. 4; CISA and FBI integrator fact sheet, as summarized by SecurityWeek - Released about 24 Sep 2026; comments due 30 Nov 2026
